q: What are the Renewable Consumption Obligation targets for each year up to 2029-30?
title: RCO targets by year, 2024-25 to 2029-30
short: The Ministry of Power notification of 27 September 2025 sets the total Renewable Consumption Obligation at 29.91% for 2024-25, 33.01% for 2025-26, 35.95% for 2026-27, 38.81% for 2027-28, 41.36% for 2028-29 and 43.33% for 2029-30, split into wind, hydro, distributed and other renewable components.
audience: Designated consumers under the Energy Conservation Act: captive users, open access consumers and their energy managers

ul: 2024-25: wind 0.67%, hydro 0.38%, distributed renewable 1.50%, other renewable 27.36%, total 29.91%.

sections.h: Which column applies to a factory
p: Paragraph 5 of the notification says open access consumers and captive users that are designated consumers meet the total obligation from any renewable source. The component split matters to distribution licensees; for a captive or open access factory the number to plan against is the total column.
The percentage is applied to electricity consumed from sources other than the discom, after the exclusions the notification lists for captive users. Nuclear power is excluded for everyone.

The September 2025 notification supersedes the earlier RCO notification S.O. 4617(E) of 20 October 2023. For designated consumers, it also says no additional Renewable Purchase Obligation applies under the Electricity Act, 2003, and state RPO targets are subsumed within these numbers.

example.title: Worked example: renewable units a captive user needs in 2026-27
lines: Consumption from sources other than the discom, after exclusions: 100 million units (MU)
Any shortfall: covered by RECs or the buyout price set by CERC

senseible: Senseible keeps your bills split by source, so the units from the discom, from captive plants and from open access stay separate. That split is the starting point for working out which consumption the RCO percentage applies to.
